title: Recording: Out On The Streets, Can She Do It Like She Dances? by Ringo Starr | 1977
content:
Atlantic Studios, New York City
Producer: Arif Mardin
Engineer: Lew Hahn

Ringo Starr recorded two songs for his sixth studio album, Ringo The 4th, on 31 January 1977.

‘Out On The Streets’ was written by Starr and Vini Poncia, one of six such collaborations on the album.

As with ‘Gave It All Up’, the song appears to be semi-autobiographical. The lyrics depict a man down on his luck, pondering his life choices: “I woke up this evening, my head was reeling/Nothing was happening, I had no feeling/I knew that I had to be out on the streets”.

‘Can She Do It Like She Dances’ was written by Steve Duboff and Gerry Robinson. It was first recorded by Gold Rush in 1975, but reached more prominence after New Orleans soul singer King Floyd released a version on his 1977 album Body English.
